title: Standing Rule on Concurrent Holdings per Claimant under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders
content:
**Rule.** A claimant may be subject to several elections and orders under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders at once, so the number of holdings per claimant is not capped overall. A limit applies only within each kind:

1. A new election or order is recorded only when the claimant does not already have the kind's maximum number of orders of the same kind with status requested, active or suspended; for voluntary elections the count is per claim.
2. A second election of the same kind on the same claim is never recorded; a change of mind is a revocation followed, where the change limit allows, by a new election.
3. How several orders share one payment is decided by the deduction priority rule of Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders, not by this rule.

## Basis of the count

| Element | What the rule looks at |
|---|---|
| Whose holdings | The same claimant's holdings, as shown in the Department's records |
| Which holdings | Holdings of the same kind as the new election or order (each of the six kinds is counted on its own) |
| Which statuses count | Requested, active or suspended |
| Scope for the two voluntary income tax kinds | Holdings on the same claim |
| Scope for the four agency kinds | All of the claimant's holdings of that kind |
| Limit compared against | The kind's maximum number of orders per claimant |
| When it is tested | Before the new election or order is recorded |

Because only requested, active and suspended holdings are counted, a holding of the kind that has been revoked or terminated does not count toward the kind's maximum.

## Condition — result

| Holdings of the same kind already counted | Result for the new election or order |
|---|---|
| Fewer than the kind's maximum | May be recorded (this count does not bar it) |
| At or above the kind's maximum | Not recorded |

## Hypothetical cases

*All cases are illustrations constructed for this rule; the maximum used is written as "the kind's maximum".*

- **Agency orders.** A claimant has two child support current support orders, one active and one suspended, and a third arrives. Both existing orders count. If two is below the kind's maximum, the third may be recorded; if it equals the maximum, it is not.
- **A terminated order.** A claimant whose only SNAP Overissuance Recovery order of a kind is terminated receives a new order of that kind. The terminated order does not count, so the count for that kind is zero.
- **Voluntary election on another claim.** A claimant with an active federal income tax election on one claim makes a federal income tax election on a different claim. The count for voluntary elections is per claim, so the election on the other claim is not counted against the new one.
- **Second election on the same claim.** A claimant with an active state income tax election on a claim asks to start another state income tax election on that same claim. A second election of the same kind on the same claim is never recorded. A change of mind is handled as a revocation of the existing election followed, where the change limit allows, by a new election.
- **Different kinds at once.** A claimant may simultaneously hold a federal election, a state election, child support orders and SNAP Overissuance Recovery orders: there is no overall cap across kinds.
